finding.claim: Authorization bypass: wipe() calls requireRole(), which only returns a boolean and never throws, and discards the result. Any authenticated user can wipe any tenant without the OWNER role.
finding.source: Any authenticated caller of POST /tenants/{t}/wipe, with arbitrary roles and an arbitrary tenant path parameter.
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27 (destructive deletion of tenant data).

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) is the handler for POST /tenants/{t}/wipe; tenant comes from the request path.
requireRole is documented to return a boolean and not throw, despite its name suggesting enforcement.
The boolean result of requireRole(u, "OWNER") is ignored, so no check is enforced.

finding.guards_checked: Looked for other checks on the path (an exception, an if on the return value, or a framework-level guard). None exist in the file. Compare export() at line 32, which correctly uses the throwing checkRole(). No other source files are present.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole() at src/Admin.java:14 returns a boolean and does not throw, and its result is discarded at line 26. checkRole() at line 18 does throw, but only export() calls it (line 32). No other guard exists.
verdict.reason: src/Admin.java:26 calls the non-throwing requireRole (defined at :14-16) as a bare statement, so repo.wipe(tenant) at :27 runs for any authenticated user, unlike export() at :32, which calls the throwing checkRole.

finding.claim: Possible cross-tenant authorization failure (IDOR): the OWNER role is global, not scoped to a tenant. Any user with OWNER can export (or, once F1 is fixed, wipe) any other tenant by changing the path parameter. This depends on how roles are assigned outside this file.
finding.source: An authenticated user holding OWNER for their own tenant, supplying a different {t} in the request path.
finding.sink: repo.export(tenant) at src/Admin.java:33, and repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27.

trace.note: User has only name and roles, with no tenant binding.
checkRole verifies only that the role string is present, not that it applies to this tenant.
repo.export(tenant) is called with the attacker-supplied tenant.

finding.guards_checked: No tenant-ownership comparison exists in this file. Repo implementations and the caller are not present, so a check there could not be ruled out.

verdict.guard_found: checkRole at src/Admin.java:18-22 throws SecurityException when the "OWNER" role is missing, and export calls it at line 32. It does no tenant comparison. No other guard exists in the only file present.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: User at src/Admin.java:4 has no tenant field, checkRole at :32 tests only for the "OWNER" role string, and repo.export(tenant) at :33 receives the path value unchanged. However, the caller, the Repo implementation and the role-assignment code are not in the repo (src/Admin.java is the only file), so I can't tell whether tenant scoping is enforced elsewhere.
